Creating the eivGP R package eivGP authors 2026-09-05 1 Literate package source The explicitly ordered .Rmd chapters are the authoritative package-building source for eivGP. Their maintained computational payload is organized by general responsibility under script/newly-written-and-modified-scripts/: shared numerics and parallelism, univariate and multivariate model engines, a unified model API, application interfaces, optional competitors, and isolated reproduction workflows. Historical R scripts are clearly separated under script/legacy-code-scripts/. The package book never launches publication-scale computation. Standalone reproduction documents live under experiments/ and applications/; they call the same exported package functions used by scripts and downstream users. Render and check the package from the repository root with: litr::render("index.Rmd") devtools::check("eivGP", document = FALSE)

3 Shared foundations Numerical linear algebra, posterior diagnostics, scoring rules, deterministic parallel mapping, validation helpers, and versioned reproduction data are shared by both model engines.

4 Univariate latent-input model This reusable engine handles one latent continuous input represented by one ordinal proxy, together with any number of numeric predictors. Study I is one configured use of this model; the fitting and prediction code itself is not study-specific.

5 Multivariate latent-input model This reusable engine handles a multivariate latent state measured through multiple noisy ordinal proxies, together with multivariate numeric predictors. Study II is one configured use of this model; the posterior, prediction, and diagnostic code is available to general package users.

6 Competitor interfaces The UC-GP, LVGP, and EzGP adapters use the public package implementations and record package versions, optimization attempts, and predictive uncertainty. They remain optional dependencies and are required only for strict publication runs.

7 Unified model API Users fit either scientific engine through fit_eivgp(), predict supported statistical targets through predict_eivgp() or predict(), and obtain latent input draws through impute_eivgp(). Published competitors have matching package-facing wrappers. utils::globalVariables(c( "block", "chain", "chain_label", "count", "draw", "ess", "global_u_accept_total", "global_u_eval_total", "global_u_total", "ref", "rhat", "theta_eval_total", "theta_update_total", "u_ess_accept_total", "u_ess_eval_total", "rank_bin", "u_ess_total", "value", "xintercept" ))

8 Compatibility API run_mixedgp_experiment() is retained for existing examples and historical workflows. The paper’s frozen publication design uses the newer study-specific runners in the next chapter.

9 Reproduction workflows The current publication workflow has one configuration constructor and one runner per study. Configurations freeze design cells, seeds, eligible methods, MCMC controls, checksums, and diagnostic gates. Both runners default to a read-only dry run. Smoke and publication fits automatically run the exact published-competitor and paired-design validators before data generation or fitting. External competitor failures are retained as auditable status records without preventing EIV-GP MCMC. The EIV-GP convergence gate is always computed and archived, but a fit that reaches its finite iteration cap below target is a warning rather than a reason to discard all later frozen replications or cells. Actual execution errors still stop the affected cell immediately. The exact scripts hashed and sourced by the publication engine are installed with the package. This preserves the same source-identity checks when eivGP is called outside a development checkout. Validator outputs and their status are written under the fingerprinted run’s config/ directory. fit <- eivGP::fit_eivgp( X, y, C, U_obs, engine = "multivariate", latent_dim = 2L, kernel = "matern" ) mean_draws <- eivGP::predict_eivgp( fit, new_X = X_new, new_C = C_new, target = "mean" ) response_draws <- predict( fit, new_X = X_new, new_C = C_new, target = "response" ) latent_draws <- eivGP::impute_eivgp(fit, new_C = C_new)

10 Application interface The real-data layer accepts arbitrary numeric predictors, ordinal proxies, and an optional sparse calibration matrix. It exposes no data download or hidden path behavior. The developing application has a standalone R Markdown file under applications/ and will remain separate from the simulation studies.

11 Package tests The canonical test file exercises public validation, fitted-object contracts, prediction targets, deterministic parallel behavior, frozen-data integrity, and installed experiment resource discovery.

12 Documentation Documentation and the namespace are generated only after every canonical module and test resource has been installed. Run the full package check separately so the literate render cannot launch or mask a check failure: study1 <- eivGP::run_study1_simulation( eivGP::study1_simulation_config(mode = "publication", workers = 8L) ) study2 <- eivGP::run_study2_simulation( eivGP::study2_simulation_config(mode = "publication", workers = 8L) )
